title: A finite module killed elementwise by a multiplicative set is killed by one element of it
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset and $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] such that $S^{-1}M=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], i.e. for every $m\in M$ there is $t\in S$ with $tm=0$. Then there is $s\in S$ with $sM=0$ (that is, $sm=0$ for all $m\in M$).

source.place: Exercises, Exercise 076A (exercise-localize-finite-module-zero, line 745: finite M with S^{-1}M=0 has f in S with M_f=0; the form sM=0 is the one used in the proof of Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 07FC, smoothing.tex line 2301: 'Hence we can find an s in S such that s annihilates Q'). Tag verified in tags/tags: 076A,exercises-exercise-localize-finite-module-zero

proof.text: Since $M$ is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], choose $m_1,\dots,m_n\in M$ ($n\ge 0$) such that every $m\in M$ can be written $m=\sum_{i=1}^n a_im_i$ with $a_i\in A$.

source.place: Exercise 076A (exercise-localize-finite-module-zero), stated without proof; the form sM=0 as used in smoothing.tex, proof of Lemma 07FC

proof.text: For each $i$, $m_i/1=0$ in $S^{-1}M=0$; by the description of the kernel of the localization map in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] ($m/1=0$ iff $um=0$ for some $u\in S$; this is the hypothesis as phrased in the statement) there is $t_i\in S$ with $t_im_i=0$.

source.place: Exercise 076A (exercise-localize-finite-module-zero), stated without proof; the form sM=0 as used in smoothing.tex, proof of Lemma 07FC

proof.text: Put $s=t_1t_2\cdots t_n$ ($s=1$ if $n=0$); $s\in S$ since $S$ is multiplicative and contains $1$. For $m=\sum_i a_im_i\in M$, commutativity of $A$ gives $sm=\sum_i a_i\big(\prod_{j\ne i}t_j\big)(t_im_i)=0$. Hence $sM=0$.

split_report.summary: Re-searched Mathlib with LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, local_search and grep: Mathlib has LocalizedModule.subsingleton_iff (S^{-1}M=0 iff every m is killed by some r in S, the node's phrasing) but the uniform annihilator for finite M only for S = p.primeCompl (Module.mem_support_iff_of_finite, LocalizedModule.exists_subsingleton_away) and S = R⁰ (Submodule.annihilator_top_inter_nonZeroDivisors); no general-S statement, so not a leaf. Split into three elementary steps (generators m_i, t_i m_i = 0 from the kernel of m -> m/1, s = prod t_i). Stacks 076A is an exercise without proof and states the conclusion as M_f = 0 for some f in S, which is equivalent (f^k M = 0 with f^k in S) and weaker-looking than the node's sM = 0; the node's form is the one used in 07FC. Statement unchanged; stmt_deps unchanged.
